The supersaturated state with an increased solid solution limit can increase the solid solution reinforcement effect, which is thought to have contributed to the strength improvement of the As-SLM group.

These tensile residual stresses are known to accelerate the generation and progression of cracks ( Edwards and Ramulu, 2014 ).

Heat treatment at 750 °C caused an increase in the ratio of the HCP phase; however, this decreased as the heat treatment temperature increased further; the ratio of the FCC phase varied correspondingly.
Heat treatment reduced the residual stress of the specimens. The residual stress of the SLM 750 group was approximately 93% less than that of the As-SLM group for Ψ = 0.

In the As-SLM group, tensile residual stress values were observed. The residual stress in the direction perpendicular to the building ( Ψ = 90) was observed to be approximately 2.4 times higher than that in the building direction ( Ψ = 0).
